key_insight: A roll-to-roll embossing-calendering process can rapidly pattern porous Prussian blue analog electrodes with tapered, isometric micro-interdigitated flow fields that improve electrolyte distribution and desalination performance.
engineering_relevance: The method preserves active material while enabling scalable, low-force fabrication of precision transport architectures for electrochemical separations and related porous-electrode devices.
method: Embossed channels into porous PBA electrodes by controlled plastic deformation during calendering.
Designed ebc-IDFFs with continuous width tapering and isometric flow paths.
Used indentation experiments and a closed-form model to quantify embossing force and local densification.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~100x faster patterning than mechanical milling, ~15x lower force than stamping, and desalination performance near potable levels with 1.5x thermodynamic energy efficiency and water recovery.
watch_item: Scalability is promising, but long-term durability and performance consistency under repeated roll-to-roll processing and real feed conditions still need validation.
paper_title: Embossing of Tapered, Isometric Micro-Interdigitated Flow Fields for Enhanced Desalination by Faradaic Deionization
